title: 1-2-3 Conjecture on neighbor-sum-distinguishing edge-weightings
statement: Let $G$ be a graph with no isolated edge. A **neighbor-sum-distinguishing (nsd) $3$-edge-weighting** is a mapping from $E(G)$ to $\{1,2,3\}$ such that the sums of the weights incident to any two adjacent vertices are distinct. **1-2-3 Conjecture.** Every graph with no isolated edge admits an nsd $3$-edge-weighting. The conjecture is a central graph-labeling problem; the source notes that an nsd $5$-edge-weighting is known, but does not state that the conjecture has been resolved.
source_name: Eranda Dhananjaya and Wei-Tian Li, “Every connected graph admits a local antimagic orientation and almost every graph admits an antimagic orientation”, arXiv:2402.10472 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10472

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).
